key_insight: Sample-based Krylov Quantum Diagonalization (SKQD) can estimate ground states of frustrated Heisenberg spin systems without variational optimization, achieving very high accuracy on small lattices and scaling to much larger systems than prior quantum approaches.
engineering_relevance: This work shows a hardware-compatible quantum workflow for strongly correlated magnets that can serve as a benchmark and a practical path toward larger frustrated spin simulations.
method: Applied SKQD to antiferromagnetic XXZ Heisenberg models on J1–J2 square, Kagome, and 1D chain lattices.
Used a ZZ deformation with Δ=2 to make the Hamiltonian sufficiently sparse for the method.
Added canonical bitstring compression and multiple Krylov subspaces to improve recovery and ground-state coverage without extra quantum resources.
evidence_signal: The paper reports sub-percent energy errors up to 24 spins, including 0.002% relative error on the 12-site Kagome lattice, and extends runs to 72 spins with errors rising to about 19%–36% at the largest size.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades substantially beyond 24 spins, so performance appears constrained by shot budget and circuit depth rather than the algorithm itself.
paper_title: Ground-state estimation of the Heisenberg model on frustrated lattices with Sample-based Krylov Quantum Diagonalization
